title: The Authority Gap: Claims, Verification, and Accountable Use in Agentic AI
description: A generated claim, a record of its evaluation, and permission to act on it are different objects. Confusing them allows an output to appear verified without the supporting process. We call this failure counterfeit descent: a claimed evaluation status unsupported by the declared checks and evidence. This paper proposes a contract for recording proposals, provenance, evaluators, unresolved obligations, and authorization decisions. Its mathematical content is narrower: finite counterexamples to composition of local acceptance, a characterization of zero conditional failure rate, and elementary verification-backlog accounting. In particular, zero local-pass/global-fail rate requires acceptance soundness on the accepted population; it does not require a boundary representation to retain every distinction relevant elsewhere. We apply these distinctions to research-paper ingestion, where file integrity, equation fidelity, proof validity, and empirical support require separate records. The reference software checks finite examples and packet consistency. It does not establish the truth of arbitrary claims, authenticate institutional authority, or measure deployment safety.
